question_html: P Ltd. has 60% voting right in Q Ltd. Q Ltd. has 20% voting right in R Ltd. Also, P Ltd. directly enjoys voting right of 14% in R Ltd. R Ltd. is a Listed Company and regularly supplies goods to P Ltd. The Management of R Ltd. has not disclosed its relationship with P Ltd. While preparing Financial Statements of P Ltd., which entities would you disclose as related parties with reference to AS-18?

options.D: Neither of Q Ltd. or R Ltd.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Q Ltd. and R Ltd. — Q Ltd. is a subsidiary of P Ltd. (P Ltd. controls >50% of its voting power), a related party outright. AS 18 defines "control"/"substantial interest" as direct or indirect ownership without dilution through a controlled subsidiary — since P Ltd. controls Q Ltd., Q Ltd.'s full 20% stake in R Ltd. is attributed to P Ltd.'s group interest. Combined with the direct 14%, the group holds 34% of R Ltd. — past AS 18's 20% substantial-interest threshold — making R Ltd. a related party too, regardless of R Ltd. management's own non-disclosure.
topic_text: AS 18 (4.3): Significant influence via combined direct and full (non-diluted) indirect voting power held through a controlled subsidiary

question_html: According to AS-18 Related Party Disclosures, which ONE of the following is not a related party of Skyline Limited?

options.A: A shareholder of Skyline Limited owning 30% of the ordinary share capital.
options.B: An entity providing banking facilities to Skyline Limited in the normal course of business.
options.D: Key management personnel of Skyline Limited.

answer_html: Answer: (B) An entity providing banking facilities to Skyline Limited in the normal course of business — AS 18 specifically excludes providers of finance, utilities, statutory bodies and similar parties from the related-party definition solely because of a normal-course-of-business relationship, even where that relationship involves significant transaction volume, provided there is no economic dependency beyond an ordinary customer/supplier relationship.
topic_text: AS 18 (4.4): Who is NOT deemed a related party under AS 18 - providers of finance/utilities in the normal course of business

case_facts_html:
Beloved Finance Ltd. is a financial enterprise which is in the business of lending loan to small businesses and earn interest on loans. During the year the Company has lend 50 crores and earned ₹1.5 crore as interest on loans. The Company had surplus funds during the year and invested then in Fixed Deposits with bank and earned interest on fixed deposits of ₹20 lacs. The Company also acquired a gold loan unit for ₹10 crore during the year and the Company provided interest free loan of ₹15 crore to its wholly-owned subsidiary. The Company paid a total income tax of ₹75 lacs for the year.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions.
question_html: Is any specific disclosures required to make in relation to the interest free loan of ₹15 crore provided by the Company to its wholly-owned subsidiary, if yes, as per which Accounting Standard:

options.A: Yes, disclosure is required to be made as per AS 3, Cash Flow Statements.
options.B: Yes, disclosure is required to be made as per AS 18, Related Party Disclosures
options.C: Yes, disclosure is required to be made as per AS 13, Accounting for Investments

answer_html: Answer: (B) — a wholly-owned subsidiary is a related party, and an interest-free loan to it is a related-party transaction outside normal market terms, so it requires specific disclosure under AS 18 (nature of relationship, transaction type/volume, and terms including the interest-free element).
topic_text: AS 18 (4.7): Disclosure requirement for a related-party transaction (interest-free loan to a wholly-owned subsidiary)

question_html: P Ltd. has 60% voting right in Q Ltd. Q Ltd. has 20% voting right in R Ltd. Also, P Ltd. directly enjoys voting right of 14% in R Ltd. R Ltd. is a Listed Company and regularly supplies goods to P Ltd. The Management of R Ltd. has not disclosed its relationship with P Ltd. While preparing Financial Statements of P Ltd., which entities would you disclose as related parties with reference to AS-18?

options.D: Neither of Q Ltd. or R Ltd.

answer_html: Answer: (c) Q Ltd. and R Ltd. — Q Ltd. is a subsidiary of P Ltd. (P Ltd. controls >50% of its voting power), so Q Ltd. is a related party outright. AS 18 defines both "control" and "substantial interest" as direct or indirect ownership of the relevant voting-power threshold — since P Ltd. controls Q Ltd. outright, Q Ltd.'s full 20% voting stake in R Ltd. is attributed to P Ltd.'s group interest without dilution (indirect holdings through a controlled subsidiary are not multiplied through the parent's ownership percentage). Combined with P Ltd.'s own direct 14%, the group holds 34% of R Ltd. — well past AS 18's 20% substantial-interest/significant-influence threshold — making R Ltd. a related party too, regardless of R Ltd. management's own non-disclosure.

question_html: PQR Ltd. sold machinery worth ₹2 crores to its subsidiary STU Pvt. Ltd. at arm's length price, paid ₹50 lakhs remuneration to its CEO/CFO, and received a ₹1 crore loan from its holding company LMN Ltd. All disclosed separately in notes to accounts. Which statement correctly reflects the application of AS 18 in this scenario?

options.A: AS 18 does not apply to transactions with subsidiaries.
options.B: Remuneration paid to CEO and CFO need not be disclosed under AS 18.
options.C: AS 18 requires disclosure of related party transactions such as sale of machinery, loans, and managerial remuneration.
options.D: AS 18 applies only to financial institutions and banks.

answer_html: Answer: (C) — AS 18 requires disclosure of related party transactions regardless of price (arm's length pricing does not exempt disclosure), including transactions with subsidiaries, holding companies, and key management personnel remuneration.
topic_text: AS 18 (4.7): Disclosure required regardless of pricing terms, covering subsidiary/holding transactions and KMP remuneration

question_html: P Ltd. has 60% voting right in Q Ltd. Q Ltd. has 20% voting right in R Ltd. Also, P Ltd. directly enjoys voting right of 14% in R Ltd. R Ltd. is a Listed Company and regularly supplies goods to P Ltd. The Management of R Ltd. has not disclosed its relationship with P Ltd. While preparing Financial Statements of P Ltd., which entities would you disclose as related parties with reference to AS-18?

options.D: Neither of Q Ltd. or R Ltd.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Q Ltd. and R Ltd. — P Ltd. holds 60% of Q Ltd., making Q Ltd. a subsidiary and hence a related party by control. Since P Ltd. controls Q Ltd., Q Ltd.'s 20% voting power in R Ltd. is aggregated with P Ltd.'s own direct 14% holding: 20% + 14% = 34% combined voting power in R Ltd., well above the 20% threshold that gives rise to significant influence, making R Ltd. a related party too. R Ltd.'s own management not having disclosed the relationship does not change P Ltd.'s disclosure obligation, since AS 18 places the disclosure duty on the reporting enterprise regardless of the counterparty's conduct.
topic_text: AS 18 (4.3): Aggregating direct and subsidiary-held voting power to test for control/significant influence over a related party
